Finite-horizon renewal inversion transfers both statements to first returns. The complete proof handles every real positive parameter, all d>=2, and endpoints within the scope. The exact-rational standalone verifier executed and passed 249 tests, which are diagnostic only, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Hsiau–Tsai–Yao theorem treats precisely the weighted sign-symmetric nearest-neighbor walks but compares first-return distributions under majorization; it neither characterizes equality of finite prefixes nor proves a sharp inverse cutoff. Belmans–Galkin–Mukhopadhyay analyze general support and construct equal-period counterexamples, including a symmetric different-weight square-support pair, outside the strict cross-polytope support here. Zhou proves full-return uniqueness for symmetric primitive walks on Z, not d-dimensional finite observation counts. Actual broader return-moment and lattice inverse-spectral searches did not locate a theorem implying the d−1 finite threshold with generic necessity. Its Bessel/Newton ingredients are classical; possible unindexed implicit coverage remains a documented risk, and absence from search results is not a proof of priority.
residual_risks: Classical lattice-walk moment and modified Bessel product literature might contain an uncatalogued identifiability theorem or one implying the finite cutoff; no search can certify nonexistence.
Unindexed general theorems on positive roots, constrained power-sum reconstruction or inverse spectral moments might immediately subsume the monotone last-coefficient step.
The full class of symmetric finite-range walks has counterexamples; the nearest-neighbor fixed-support hypothesis cannot be relaxed by these arguments.
No independent correctness or priority audit has been performed.

value.rationale: An explicitly active lattice-walk inverse problem and a recent first-return study motivate determining whether finitely many observables recover anisotropic transition weights. The theorem answers a natural complete inverse classification on the known nearest-neighbor family, not a hand-picked numeric slice: exactly d−1 moments are sufficient, a generic smooth d−2-observation ambiguity makes the bound optimal, and a monotone scalar equation supplies constructive recovery. The source work supplies forward dominance and broad non-identifiability counterexamples, neither this sharp inverse threshold. The additional probability normalization is essential beyond bare power sums. No claims about noisy identifiability, unknown supports or higher-value downstream theorems are needed.
